'''John Courtney "Jack" Decius''' (1920 – 1994) was an American [[Physical chemistry|physical chemist]], [[Molecular spectroscopy|molecular spectroscopist]], and [[Research|researcher]] on the faculty of [[Oregon State College]].  He made significant contributions to the study of [[Vibrational spectroscopy of linear molecules|vibrational spectra]], [[dipole]] and [[ion]] interactions, and [[Infrared spectroscopy|infrared]] and [[Raman spectroscopy]] of [[Crystal|crystals]] and [[Ion speciation|ionic species.]] 

== Early life and education ==
John C. Decius was born Feb. 13, 1920, in [[San Francisco]], the son of Lewis Courtney Decius and Grace (Towne) Decius. In 1941 he took his [[baccalaureate degree]] in chemistry at [[Stanford University|Stanford]], and in 1947 earned his Ph.D. at [[Harvard University|Harvard]],<ref name=":1">{{Cite news |date=1994-09-09 |title=Obituary for John C. Decius (Aged 74) |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/corvallis-gazette-times-obituary-for-joh/38729344/ |access-date=2026-09-30 |work=Corvallis Gazette-Times |pages=3}}</ref> with a dissertation titled, ''I. Vibrational Potential Functions for Several Halomethanes and Halo-Ethanes II. The Principles of Dimensional Analysis and Scaled Models'', advised by [[Edgar Bright Wilson]].<ref>Decius, John Courtney. ''I. Vibrational Potential Functions for Several Halomethanes and Halo-Ethanes II. The Principles of Dimensional Analysis and Scaled Models''. Source: Doctoral Dissertations Accepted by American Universities 1933-1955, 1946/1947, volume 14, page 25 American Doctoral Dissertations, Source code: W1947, page: 0025.</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Decius |first=John Courtney |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/I_Vibrational_Potential_Functions_for_Se/UI0YHAAACAAJ?hl=en |title=I. Vibrational Potential Functions for Several Halo-methanes and Halo-ethanes. Part Two: The Principles of Dimentional Analysis and Scaled Models |date=1947 |publisher=Harvard University |language=en}}</ref>

Decius married Anne Streeter in 1948, and they raised a son, Peter S. Decius, and daughters Joyce S. Decius Lowry and Sylvia Russell. They had three grandchildren.<ref name=":1" />

Decius died in 1994, due to injuries sustained in an auto accident.<ref name=":1" />

== Career ==
Decius became a professor of chemistry at Oregon State College in 1949.<ref name=":1" /> He retired as a designated "Distinguished Professor" in 1981.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |date=2013-08-14 |title=OSU Alumni Association Distinguished Professor Award Previous Recipients |url=https://senate.oregonstate.edu/osu-alumni-association-distinguished-professor-award-previous-recipients |access-date=2026-09-30 |website=senate.oregonstate.edu |language=en}}</ref>
